summary: Cloud scan of https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com complete. Found 2 critical and 3 high vulnerabilities.

findings.title: AWS Credentials and Database URL Leak
findings.description: The application's `.env` file is publicly accessible, exposing sensitive environment variables. This includes hypothetical AWS access keys, a database connection string with credentials, and a Stripe API key. Such exposure allows an attacker to gain unauthorized access to AWS resources, the application's database, and payment processing functionalities, potentially leading to data exfiltration, service compromise, or financial fraud.
findings.recommendation: Restrict public access to `.env` files. Ensure web server configurations (e.g., Nginx, Apache) explicitly deny access to dotfiles or sensitive configuration files. Store sensitive credentials securely in environment variables or a dedicated secret management service (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) and avoid hardcoding or exposing them in files accessible via the web server.

findings.title: Git Repository Disclosure
findings.evidence:
[core]
	repositoryformatversion = 0
	filemode = true
	bare = false
	logallrefupdates = true
	ignorecase = true
[remote "origin"]
	url = git@github.com:OWASP/JuiceShop.git
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*
[branch "main"]
	remote = origin
	merge = refs/heads/main
findings.description: The `.git` directory of the application is publicly accessible, allowing an attacker to download the entire repository (e.g., via tools like `git-dumper`). This exposes the application's source code, internal configurations, developer comments, and potentially other sensitive information. This can be used to identify further vulnerabilities, reverse-engineer proprietary logic, or exploit hidden functionalities, leading to full application compromise.
findings.recommendation: Restrict public access to the `.git` directory. Configure the web server to deny access to `.git` and its contents. Ensure that `.git` directories are not deployed to production environments or are properly secured if they must be present (e.g., by placing them outside the web root).

findings.title: Broken Object Level Auth
findings.evidence: Access to sensitive data without token
findings.description: The API endpoint `/api/users/{id}` is vulnerable to Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA). An attacker can manipulate the `{id}` parameter in the URL to access sensitive profile data (e.g., email, address, security questions) of other users, including administrative users, without proper authorization checks. This bypass allows unauthorized data disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Implement robust object-level authorization checks on all API endpoints that handle object IDs. Ensure that the server-side logic strictly validates if the authenticated user is explicitly authorized to access the specific object requested. This typically involves comparing the object owner's ID with the authenticated user's ID or verifying administrative privileges before returning sensitive data.

findings.title: HSTS Missing — Forces HTTPS
findings.evidence: HTTP Response did not contain 'Strict-Transport-Security' header. Status: 200
findings.description: The response from https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com is missing the 'Strict-Transport-Security' security header.
findings.recommendation: Add the 'Strict-Transport-Security' header to all server responses.
